title: System Protocol 1: String Command
lessonSummary: Perfect! With f-strings you fuse text and variables into precise messages.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: three f-strings with variables and a calculation.
tasks.codeTemplate:
# Example 1: Simple f-strings
pilot = "Zara"
rank = 5
print(f"Hello {pilot}!")
print(f"Your rank: {rank}")

# Example 2: With calculations
energy_a = 75
energy_b = 25
print(f"Total energy: {energy_a + energy_b}%")

# Example 3: Multiple variables
ship = "Nebula-Falcon"
captain = "Orion"
mission = "Expedition Alpha"
print(f"{ship} under {captain} launches {mission}!")

validation.expected: Nebula-Falcon under Orion launches Expedition Alpha!

tasks.instruction: Create the variables pilot = "Nova" and rank = 7. Use an f-string to print exactly: Commander Nova, rank 7
Create energy_a = 60 and energy_b = 25. Let an f-string do the calculation and print exactly: Total energy: 85%

title: System Protocol 2: Strings and type()
lessonSummary: Text data decoded! type() reveals the quantum type of any information.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the quantum type of the ship name.
Create planet = "Mars" and print its quantum type with type().
Create ship_class = "Cruiser" and print exactly: Class: Cruiser, type: <class 'str'> (let the f-string fill in the type with type()).

title: System Protocol 3: Integers
lessonSummary: Whole numbers under control! Crew and decks are counted with int.

tasks.instruction: Run this example with two integers.
Create crew_count = 300 and deck_count = 12 and print exactly: Crew: 300, Decks: 12
Create deck_count = 12 and print its quantum type with type().

title: System Protocol 4: Floats
lessonSummary: Precision achieved! Floats store decimal numbers for exact measurements.

tasks.instruction: Run this example with two floats.
tasks.codeTemplate:
speed = 2.5
coordinate_x = 127.35
print(f"Speed: {speed} light years/h")
print(f"Position X: {coordinate_x}")
print(f"Type: {type(speed)}")

tasks.instruction: Create speed = 3.7 and coordinate_x = 88.25 and print exactly: Position X: 88.25
Create speed = 3.7 and print its quantum type with type().

title: System Protocol 5: Booleans
lessonSummary: System states decoded! A Boolean is always either True or False.

tasks.instruction: Run this example with two system states.
tasks.codeTemplate:
system_online = True
alarm_active = False
print(f"System online: {system_online}")
print(f"Alarm active: {alarm_active}")
print(f"Type: {type(system_online)}")

tasks.instruction: Create shield_active = True and reactor_overheated = False and print exactly: Shield active: True
Create alarm_active = False and print its quantum type with type().
Print the result of the comparison 80 > 50 directly with print().

title: System Protocol 6: Operations
lessonSummary: Calculations and text fusion mastered – the data lab runs at full power!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: calculations and text operations.
tasks.codeTemplate:
# Mathematical operations
planets_a = 8
planets_b = 4
print(f"Total planets: {planets_a + planets_b}")
print(f"Difference: {planets_a - planets_b}")
print(f"Doubled: {planets_a * 2}")
print(f"Per sector: {planets_a / 2}")

# String operations
prefix = "Neo"
suffix = "tron"
system_name = prefix + suffix
print(f"System name: {system_name}")
print(f"Signal: {prefix * 3}")

tasks.instruction: Create planets = 9. Print exactly: Per sector: 3.0 (divide the planets by 3 inside an f-string).
Join "Star" and "lab" with + into a variable system_name and print exactly: System name: Starlab
Repeat the text "Ping" three times with * and print the result.

title: System Protocol 7: Type Conversion
lessonSummary: Transformation complete! int(), float(), str() and bool() convert any data.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: convert text into numbers.
tasks.codeTemplate:
temperature_str = "273"
temperature_int = int(temperature_str)
print(f"Temperature as text: {temperature_str}K (type: {type(temperature_str)})")
print(f"Temperature as number: {temperature_int}K (type: {type(temperature_int)})")

# Process sensor data
sensor_value = "42.5"
value_float = float(sensor_value)
print(f"Sensor value {value_float} doubled: {value_float * 2}")

tasks.instruction: Create temperature_str = "300", convert it with int() and print exactly: Temperature plus 10: 310K
Create sensor_value = "12.5", convert it with float() and print exactly: Sensor value tripled: 37.5
Create crew = 12 and join it with + into this line, using str(): Crew: 12

lessonSummary: Fleet analysed – total strength and average speed determined!

title: Mission 3: The Asteroid Mining
lessonSummary: Mining decision made – the more valuable asteroid gets mined!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create variables for both asteroids and calculate both raw values (value_a and value_b). Print two lines in the format Ceres-9 value: 5000.0 – the last line must read: Vesta-3 value: 5400.0
Step 2 – Compare the values (start from value_a = 5000.0 and value_b = 5400.0): store value_b > value_a in a Boolean variable b_is_better and print exactly: Vesta-3 is more valuable: True
Step 3 – Calculate the average value of both asteroids and print exactly: Average value: 5200.0 – then print your mining decision: Mining decision: Vesta-3

title: Extra challenge 1: The Spaceship Dock
lessonSummary: Dock under control – every bay monitored!

title: Extra challenge 2: The AI Laboratory

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create variables for all three models. Print the heading === AI LAB PROTOCOL === and one f-string line per model in the format NovaNet: accuracy 0.92, 1200000 parameters (the last line must read: MiniMind: accuracy 0.75, 300000 parameters).
